questionFindings.question: National leaders should need to win regular competitive elections to remain in office.
questionFindings.rationaleAtReview: His proposed electoral reform is explicitly to be submitted through an election manifesto, affirming competitive electoral authority.

questionFindings.finalDecision: No further objection within the stated bounded source review; no publication clearance.

questionFindings.question: Every adult citizen should have the right to vote, regardless of their education or intelligence.
questionFindings.rationaleAtReview: He says the electoral system should make every vote count and every voice heard, rather than attach intelligence qualifications.
questionFindings.note: Universal vote and equal campaign conditions require a franchise/electoral-rights bridge beyond inclusive reform rhetoric. The actual speech also praises a low-education father voting: a qualified education-independent franchise inference is stronger than the current broad slogan, but exact universality remains qualified.
questionFindings.finalRationale: His conference speech explicitly describes his father failing the eleven-plus examination yet repeatedly exercising his vote, and presents that participation as valuable. This supports qualified education-independent voting rights; the speech does not expressly discuss every possible cognitive qualification, so strong agreement is not inferred.
questionFindings.finalDecision: Resolved by a weaker +1 and specific low-education father voting passage independently reread in conference text; intelligence limitation explicit.

oldVerdictReview.reason: The archived empathy comparison is independently defective: policy on social formation cannot establish comparative inherited-versus-learned empathy predominance. This finding concerns the archived rationale, independently of the sparse new replacement. Other competent historical/modern bridges must be retained.

specificEvidence.oldRationale: Conditional inference on inherited empathy capacity: the assessment balances the case that inherited variation is weighted above social formation against the case that relationships and social experience primarily shape empathy. Evidence context: Patriotic education and family socialisation are treated as shaping conduct, alongside biological health and demographic concerns. Qualification: Traditional family policy does not prove that racial heredity explains violence or national IQ; fine-grained temperament responses are conditional inferences. Neutral represents the competing considerations, not a claim that silence proves neutrality. Lower-confidence analogy: the sources establish a broader causal or risk principle, not a published answer to this particular empirical or biomedical comparison.
specificEvidence.defect: Moral solidarity, inclusive representation or integration policy cannot establish inherited versus learned empathy dominance. The archived claim introduces a psychological comparison that the cited policy rationale does not substantiate.
